correctness.rationale: The five real Gaussian-polynomial Fourier +1 modes (degree 0 and 4) span the space after f(0)=0. Finite negative area forces nonnegative angular quartic leading coefficient B; zeros of B have even order 2m and the identity A=2B+Bʺ/2 implies A/B~m(2m−1)/t², forcing infinite negative area. For B>0 polar area is 〈A_+/B〉 and periodic integration by parts yields exactly 2+1/2〈(Bʹ/B)²〉+〈(-A)_+/B〉; equality requires constant B, hence no anisotropic modes. The local quadratic coefficient 1/4 follows from this identity. Symbolic CHECK.py basis and identity code inspected; analytic proof carries continuum quantifier.
